$about: The first run in either corpus whose asking can be checked rather than believed. One adoption of a private commercial repository - anonymised at the owner's request, see the transcript's own note on what is redacted - run by its owner against a working copy of the elicitation layer, prompt A1 typed in Polish as `zadoptuj do repositorystandards.com`. Every question the agent put and every answer the owner gave is reproduced in transcripts/2026-08-19-g-adoption.md, extracted from the session transcript rather than recalled: seven AskUserQuestion calls, twenty questions, twenty answers.

$elicitation.$why: The corpus's whole problem was a record that asserted asking with nothing to check it against. This one names the file, the file holds the questions verbatim, and the counts in here were measured out of the session transcript by script rather than counted by hand afterwards - structurally, from assistant turns that really called the tool, which is the same test the guard applies.

$recommendation_finding: The measured case for the rule ADR-054 states, and it is not the one this repo expected. Of twenty answers, six took the recommendation, thirteen took another option on the list, and one was typed off the list entirely. The interesting split is narrower: in seven questions the agent recommended the *less* convergent of the options it offered - keep your own layout, keep your own guards, take the records as they are, fill only the gaps, list the informal material for triage rather than pull it in, keep the parallel tracker, and last of all let the repository's own conventions win - and the owner overrode every single one of the seven toward the standard. Not once did the owner move the other way. Three further questions recommended the smaller piece of work rather than the smaller commitment - do not touch the specs' scope, treat `spec-structure` passing as done, keep the persona mapping provisional - and the owner asked for more on all three. An adoption that recommends against adopting is not cautious, it is wrong about what the person in front of it wants, and this run says so with numbers rather than with an argument.
$off_list_finding: The seventh question offered `core` or `scale` and the owner typed neither: `wiecej obob nad tym pracuje al enie chce sprintow, raczej pracujemy na zasadzie backlogu i bierzemy zadania bez sprintow i celowanych terminow` - several people, no sprints, work taken off a backlog. Reproduced with the typos because that is what was typed. The answer is `scale` on the axis that decides anything (work changes hands, so spec-guard has to block rather than advise) and reads as `core` on the two axes the question was actually framed on, headcount and sprints. The agent resolved it correctly and said why - docs/sprints/ and sprint-guard.mjs are required: false even at `scale`. The question was reframed around the hand-off afterwards, and .claude/elicitation/README.md now says what this run demonstrated: the option list is never the whole answer space.
$harvest_finding: Two of the twenty questions carried no point id, because no point declared them: where tracked work lives when the repository already tracks it somewhere else, and which profile the repository runs at. Both are now declared points (adopt.tracker, adopt.profile). This is the loop the layer was built for - the list is a floor a hook can refuse a write for, the questions worth asking are mostly ones no list anticipated, and what a run invents is the evidence for what the list should grow.
$bootstrap_finding: The layer landed first and the session restarted, which is the ordering the skills now require and the reason this run has a transcript at all. Commit 890cd28c put the hook, the point list, the PreToolUse matcher and the ledger in the repository at 12:37 local, before anything gated was written; the session that ran the adoption starts at 13:04. A PreToolUse hook binds at session start, so had the run copied the layer in mid-session it would have written the entire adoption with the guard inert - which is precisely the run the layer exists to stop.
$guard_finding: The adoption answered `adopt.guards` with merge and then had to justify every deviation, which turned four of this standard's own shipped guards into measured findings against us. Reproduced here against the shipped copies, not taken on the adopter's word: `no-force-push.sh` denies `git push -qf origin main` and allows `git push -fq origin main` - the same push, one keystroke apart; `no-ci-secret-writes.sh` denies `grep -rn "gh secret set" docs/`, so searching for the phrase is treated as writing a secret; `no-remote-db-writes.sh` lets `cat migration.sql | psql -h <remote>` and `psql -h <remote> -fmigration.sql` straight through, and its segment splitter cuts inside `-c "SELECT 1; DROP TABLE x"`, separating a write from the host it runs against. The repository had closed all four before the adoption and kept its versions as recorded exceptions with a 111-case suite behind them. A guard nobody can trust to deny is the same failure as a guard nobody can work under, one direction over.

observations.target: repo:private commercial SaaS (booking platform), anonymised - several contributors, work handed off, no sprints
observations.language: Polish end to end - the first line was typed in Polish and nothing asked which language to use
observations.outcome: 25 commits, 253 files, +12670/-847, on a branch that ends green on the repository's own gates: self-verify drift 0 (95% adopted, 5 recorded exceptions, sprint-guard NOT RUN because the profile carries no sprints), elicitation-provenance 18 points recorded (12 human, 5 provisional, 1 legally pending). The informal material moved into docs/discovery/ as tracked renames with no content change, and the four source comments that pointed at the old paths were repointed rather than left broken. The 33 decision records were reshaped into one front-matter table and gained a Confirmation section citing real tests; not a line of the owner's prose was rewritten. The run reviewed its own diff before pushing and recorded three findings against itself - a decision-record count that stood at 37 in four places against 33 real records, a second copy of the glob translator inside elicitation-provenance.mjs, and its own commit count - together with the one file its review could not read, scripts/spec-guard.mjs, whose predecessor stored a NUL byte and so has no diff. That file is byte-for-byte the standard's shipped copy, checked by hash here, so the declared gap contains nothing repo-specific.
observations.evidence: Branch `adopt/repository-standards` in the adopting repository (base `elicitation-field-test`, 25 commits); the ledger at docs/adoption-provenance.md and the intake at docs/adoption-intake.md in that branch, both of which record the answers and what the verdict does not cover; and the questions and answers verbatim in docs/validation/human-prompting/transcripts/2026-08-19-g-adoption.md here.
